subject: Colorizing tree by clade in PCA/PhyPCA/PACA plots

messages.author: f885e974e72cf61d
messages.subject: Colorizing tree by clade in PCA/PhyPCA/PACA plots
parts:
Hi all, 

I am attempting to replicate the plots created in the Collyer & Adams (2020) PACA publication. I would like to specify clades (subfamilies) within my tree to better visualize patterns of phylogenetic and ecological signals and be able to change the points to represent other traits (e.g., diet) that are assigned in a data frame. 

I have tried: 
- the code in the supplementary materials (unclear how to translate it to an existing phylogeny/delineate clade colors or tip colors when I would like them to have a specific name/legend attached), 
- using the paintedTree function (phytools) - the result is below and close to what I'm hoping for (thought legend is incorrect), but the plot() function will not accept the tree this creates,


- using ggplot, but it will not consistently accept data directly from geomorph, so the data have to be extracted but the clade delineation issues persist,
- asking others for help and other random things

Clearly, I am missing something; I'm hoping someone can point me to a resource with a walkthrough or offer some suggestions. I would greatly appreciate it!

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Colorizing tree by clade in PCA/PhyPCA/PACA plots
parts:
Please see the help file for gm.prcomp. There is an example at the end where one colors by some groups.  Replicated in the email here:


Dean

 

data(plethspecies)

Y.gpa <- gpagen(plethspecies$land)    #GPA-alignment

PaCA.ols <- gm.prcomp(Y.gpa$coords, phy = plethspecies$phy,

                      align.to.phy = TRUE)

summary(PaCA.ols)

plot(PaCA.ols, phylo = TRUE, main = "PaCA using OLS")

 

gps <- as.factor(c(rep("gp1", 5), rep("gp2", 4))) # Two random groups

plot(PaCA.ols, pch=22, cex = 1.5, bg = gps, phylo = TRUE)

messages.author: f885e974e72cf61d
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Colorizing tree by clade in PCA/PhyPCA/PACA plots
parts:
Hi Dean,

Thanks very much for pointing me to this resource. I did look at the help file prior to posting here and had difficulty replicating it since my groups are not randomly assigned or generated. I have an imported excel file with behavioral, ecological, and phylogenetic (i.e., subfamily) data, and I have tried turning many of the individual variables into factors. Even so, I'm still unable to (1) color the branches of the phylogeny by subfamily as in your publication or (2) have the factor applied correctly to the plot. For instance, in the subfamily phyPCA plots below, the subfamily factor is not applied to the correct species. The circled species all belong to 1 subfamily. The factor is coded as such and in the order that matches the phylogenetic tree. There's clearly something I'm missing. Can you or the group please provide further guidance? 

Code:
species.phypca = gm.prcomp(species.means, phy=must.tree, align.to.phy = FALSE, GLS = TRUE)
summary(species.phypca)

species.subfamily = as.factor(EcoBehSpecies.matched$Subfamily)
plot(species.phypca, pch=22, cex = 1.5, bg = species.subfamily, phylo=TRUE, main = "PhyPCA")

Thank you,
Ani

messages.author: fbfd20ce829c6c6c
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Colorizing tree by clade in PCA/PhyPCA/PACA plots
parts:
Hi Ani, 

Just looking at your code, it looks like there is a mismatch between the order of species in the colors and the PCA scores you are giving the plot function. species.phypca comes from species.means while species.subfamily comes from EcoBehSpecies.matched$Subfamily. 

What I would do is inspect the rownames of the scores within species.phypca$x and make sure that the colors you provide match the species order as you expect them to so the colors match up when using plot(). 

Regarding your legend, I saw some colors repeated, implying that you may need to provide the legend function the levels and not a factor. Getting the legend you want may also involve reordering the levels manually, I think they are usually listed alphabetically within a factor. Or you may be able to provide text and colors/color codes yourself and make the legend manually.

Best,
Bryan
